title: A listing change has no matching MLS field
when: A signed change names a piece of data that has no valid field in the MLS record (for example lot size in acres where the MLS has no such field).
steps: Agent 05 (MLS & Listing Management) does not enter it anywhere.
It asks you, naming the data that has no valid MLS field.
never: Squeeze the data into the nearest-looking field.
why: Data in the wrong field misleads buyers and agents who search on that field.
you_see: A question naming the data with no valid MLS field.
test: A live listing; you sign a change setting lot_acres to 0.5.

title: A listing portal shows different data than the MLS
when: A syndicated portal (for example a public listing site) shows data that differs from the MLS record.
steps: Agent 05 corrects the source record first.
It then checks every portal again.
never: Patch a single portal and leave the source wrong.
why: Portals copy the MLS. Fixing the source is the only fix that sticks everywhere.
you_see: Nothing yet: this is not built.

title: Two signed listing changes contradict each other
when: Two authorized changes to the same listing conflict (for example from two people with signing authority).
steps: Agent 05 carries out neither change.
It asks you which one stands.
never: Apply the later one, or either one, without asking.
why: Two signed instructions that disagree mean one is a mistake; the listing must not change on a guess.

title: A portal is still out of date after the check window
when: A portal still shows old data after the time allowed for it to update.
steps: Agent 05 records it and tells you.
It never marks the update complete.
never: Mark an update done while a portal still shows the old data.
why: A stale price or status on a public site misleads buyers. Done means done everywhere.
you_see: Nothing yet: this is not built.

title: A status change arrives without the document it needs
when: A signed status change needs a supporting document that is missing (for example "sold" without the closing document).
steps: Agent 05 refuses the change.
It asks you for the missing document, naming it.
never: Change a status before the required document is on file.
why: A status without its proof is a false public statement about the property.
you_see: A question naming the document the change requires.
test: A live listing; you sign a change to "sold" with no closing document. No status change is carried out.

title: A status change arrives without your signature
when: A status change arrives that you did not sign (for example a verbal or emailed instruction typed in).
steps: The dispatcher refuses it before Agent 05 sees it.
It is recorded as an integrity violation and you are alerted.
never: Treat a verbal or emailed instruction as authority.
why: Only your signature can change a listing. Anything else could be a mistake or an impersonation.
you_see: An integrity alert naming the refused change.
test: A live listing; an unsigned instruction to withdraw it arrives. The status is not changed.

title: The MLS rejects an entry
when: The MLS refuses an entry on one of its rules.
steps: Agent 05 records the MLS's rejection exactly as given.
It tells you.
never: Change the data just to get past the MLS's check.
why: Bending data to pass validation creates a listing that is wrong in a way nobody chose.
you_see: Nothing yet: this is not built.

title: A signed price change disagrees with the amendment on file
when: The price in a signed change differs from the price in the listing agreement amendment on file.
steps: Agent 05 stops and does not change the price.
It asks you, naming both amounts.
never: Pick one of the two prices.
why: The listing agreement is a contract with the seller. Publishing a price it does not support is a breach risk.
you_see: A question saying the price conflicts with the agreement amendment.
test: A live listing; you sign a price of $440,000 while the amendment on file says $435,000. The price is not changed.

title: Someone asks to fill in buyer-broker compensation on the MLS
when: A change asks to fill in the buyer-broker compensation field.
steps: Agent 05 leaves the field blank: offers of compensation are not allowed on the MLS since August 17, 2024.
It raises a legal-line alert for you naming the request.
never: Fill in, or work around, the compensation field.
why: Putting a compensation offer on the MLS breaks the rules that came out of the 2024 national settlement.
you_see: A legal-line alert about the compensation request.
test: A live listing; you sign a change setting buyer_broker_comp to 2.5%.

title: The marketing copy and the MLS record disagree
when: A released description says something different from the MLS record (for example a different square footage).
steps: The MLS record is the truth.
Agent 05 sends the corrected data to Agent 04, which redrafts; the corrected copy goes through Compliance and is released again.
The discrepancy is written in the client's history.
The correction runs once; it does not loop.
never: Leave copy on the market that contradicts the MLS.
why: Two different numbers in public invite a misrepresentation claim; one source of truth avoids it.
you_see: The corrected copy; the discrepancy in the history.
test: The MLS record says 2,000 sq ft; the first description was built from the 1,800 sq ft tax record. After the correction the released copy says 2,000 sq ft and the listing goes live once.

title: A withdrawal is asked for while the listing is under contract
when: A signed withdrawal arrives for a listing that has a signed purchase contract.
steps: Agent 05 stops; the listing is not withdrawn.
It sends the matter to Compliance (Agent 17) and raises a legal-line alert for you.
never: Change a listing's status on its own while a contract is live.
why: Withdrawing during a contract can breach it. That is a legal decision, not a data change.
you_see: A legal-line alert saying a withdrawal was requested while under contract.
test: A live listing goes to pending with a signed contract; then you sign a withdrawal.

title: A vacant listing gets regular property checks
when: You mark a listing as vacant.
steps: Agent 05 starts a vacancy watch and records it.
On each daily run it asks Agent 09 (Vendor Coordination) for a property condition check.
Agent 09 books the first check; the booking waits for your release like any vendor booking.
While that check is open, Agent 09 does not book another one; it tells you once that it was not booked again.
never: Stack up duplicate check bookings while one is open.
why: Empty houses invite damage and break-ins, and insurance can depend on regular checks. One open booking at a time keeps the vendor schedule honest.
you_see: The first check booking waiting for your release; one note that further checks were not booked while it is open.
test: A vacant listing goes live. The daily clock runs on days 1, 3 and 8: Agent 05 asks three times, one check is booked, and you are told once.

title: A vacant listing is occupied again
when: A vacant listing is marked occupied, or the listing ends.
steps: Agent 05 stops the vacancy watch.
It records that the watch ended.
No further property checks are asked for.
never: Keep ordering checks for an occupied home.
why: Checks on an occupied home cost money and intrude on the people living there.
you_see: The watch's end in the client's history.
test: A vacant listing goes live; two days later you mark it occupied; the clock runs a week later and no check is asked for.
